name: 74-use-context-frontier
_comment: Owner directive 2026-10-16: frequent USE CONTEXT FRONTIER reminder for the main agent AND every subagent role, plus the standing 'nothing is a given, decide claims from as many primary sources as possible' rule.
body: [74-use-context-frontier] USE CONTEXT FRONTIER before any plan, verdict, edit to a load-bearing file or citation of existing authority, in every role and in the main agent. Nothing is a given: no claim stands on one source or on a previous message; decide it from as many primary sources as possible (the defining line, every consumer, tests, decision records) and re-seed until the frontier is closed. Tests, builds and code are not proof of working either: run what you change and observe real behaviour, render, output and logs; report what stayed unverified. Rationale, seeding and cost: periodic reminder.

remind.suffix:
[USE CONTEXT FRONTIER]

Nothing is a given. Before a plan, a verdict, an edit to a load-bearing file, or any citation of existing authority: run context_frontier with this task's seeds, read the load-bearing hits in full, and feed newly discovered entities back as seeds until the frontier is closed. A conclusion in code is a conclusion drawn from as many primary sources as possible, not from the first plausible one.

WHY IT PAYS OFF - each line is a failure it removes:
- Stops invented authority: claiming "the owner decided X" requires the actual record; the pass shows it absent in seconds instead of burning a review round on the claim.
- Finds the OWNER of a thing: a token, constant, test or decision record has one defining site and many consumers. Grep-by-memory picks the wrong file; the frontier returns the definition and every reference.
- Exposes what your change breaks: importers, callers, tests and docs that a single-file read cannot show.
- Makes self-checks falsifiable: a gate can only pass if its pattern actually matches the defect form present in the source.
- Cheap and safe: read-only, bounded, needs no graph index, never blocks the task when it fails.

TESTS AND CODE ARE NOT PROOF: green tests, a passing build, a clean typecheck and an approved reviewer verdict prove only those signals, never that the thing works. Whatever you change, RUN it and watch the real thing: the rendered output, the real request, the real process, the logs - at the conditions the owner actually cares about. If it cannot be run, say so and name what stays unverified instead of reporting it done.

HOW TO SEED IT: rare identifiers win - $tokens, symbols, DEC/claim ids, file paths. Common class or component names flood the output (up to 60 files per identifier) and get skipped as noise; 3-5 sharp seeds return about 10 relations, 7 loose ones return 100.

Its output is candidates, not semantics: it proves text presence, never meaning. Read what is load-bearing, explicitly discard the rest.

And what you read is still only source, not proof of behaviour: the closure pass tells you what to change, the run tells you whether it works.
